rows: Alteration, demolition and dismantling must avoid unplanned structural collapse.
A competent person should survey and assess the structure before load-bearing elements are altered.
Assessment should consider age, construction type, previous use and nearby structures.
Temporary support should be designed for foreseeable loads.
Temporary support must be installed, inspected and maintained as designed.
Changing load paths and demolition sequence must be considered.
Facade retention and restraint systems require competent design and control.
Workers and passers-by must be protected from collapse and debris.
A building drawing or visual condition report does not prove structural stability during alteration.
Conclusions require survey, load paths, sequence, temporary works, condition, monitoring and competent-design evidence.
COSHH aims to prevent or adequately control exposure to hazardous substances.
Elimination or substitution should be considered before relying on lower-order controls.
Enclosure and local exhaust ventilation can reduce exposure at source.
Work procedures, supervision and training are part of exposure control.
Control measures should be used correctly by workers.
Maintenance, examination and testing are required where controls could deteriorate.
Work frequency, timing and the number of people exposed can be adjusted to reduce risk.
Respiratory protection may be needed where other measures cannot adequately control exposure.
A safety data sheet or substance name does not establish actual worker exposure.
Exposure conclusions require substance, task, route, amount, controls, duration, maintenance and monitoring evidence.
Respiratory protective equipment should be selected for the hazard and required protection.
The assigned protection factor must be adequate for the exposure scenario.
RPE should be compatible with the task and other personal protective equipment.
Tight-fitting facepieces require an adequate seal to the wearer.
Face-fit testing is required for relevant tight-fitting RPE.
Users need training in fitting, use, checks and limitations.
Filters and breathing apparatus should be used within their specified limits.
RPE must be stored, cleaned, maintained and replaced as necessary.
A mask model or fit-test record does not prove protection during a particular task.
Protection conclusions require contaminant, concentration, APF, fit, wear time, filter, maintenance and user evidence.
Employers must provide adequate ventilation in enclosed workplaces.
Ventilation should supply fresh or purified air and remove stale indoor air.
Poorly ventilated areas should be identified through workplace assessment.
Natural ventilation can use doors, windows, vents and grilles.
Mechanical ventilation uses fans and ducts to move air.
Mixed natural and mechanical arrangements may be appropriate.
Ventilation should reflect occupancy, room use and pollutant sources.
Ventilation systems should be maintained so they continue to perform.
A window count or design specification does not prove adequate ventilation during use.
Conclusions require airflow, occupancy, room volume, source, operation, maintenance and measured-condition evidence.
